modules.title: 重复实现带来什么改动负担

items.title: 失败前：五个文件分别保存样式
items.text: 要统一改按钮颜色，就得找到五处定义；漏掉文档页时，那里的按钮仍是灰色。

items.title: 改动来源：共享组件
items.text: 按项目现有结构把按钮样式放在一个共享组件，五个页面都从这里取得样式。

items.title: 反馈与边界
items.text: 改完重新打开五个页面，确认按钮都变蓝且没有其它显示回归；是否继续整理，要看实际改动负担，不是所有重复代码都要立刻重写。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 重复代码不一定都要合并；当这次改色已经漏掉一个页面、以后每次仍要逐个找五份来源时，维护负担就有了具体表现。共享之前也要确认页面差异不是有意保留的。

lessonPractice.title: 五份按钮样式改成蓝色后，四页已变色但文档页仍灰。这次漏改说明什么？

options.label: 按钮有五份独立定义；相同改动必须逐处更新，一处漏改就会不一致
options.feedback: 对。五个独立来源让相同样式需要同步多处；页面复查发现一处还停留在旧值。

options.label: 按钮其实共用一个来源，只是文档页还缓存着旧页面
options.feedback: 示例明确有五份独立定义；浏览器缓存不能解释这些副本为什么需要逐个修改。

options.label: 文档页的灰色是刻意设计的权限状态，不需要对照改动记录
options.feedback: 示例里没有权限或设计差异的依据；文档页漏掉了本次明确的颜色改动。

en.title: Five button styles were changed to blue, but four pages are blue while Docs is still gray. What does this miss show?

options.label: There are five independent definitions; the same change must be applied at each source, so one can be missed
options.feedback: Correct. Five separate sources mean the same style change must be synchronized in several places; checking the pages exposed one stale value.

options.label: The button has one shared source, but Docs is still showing a cached page
options.feedback: The example has five independent definitions; browser cache does not explain why those copies need separate edits.

options.label: The gray Docs button is an intentional permission state, so ignore the change record
options.feedback: The example gives no evidence for a permission or design difference; Docs missed the explicitly requested color change.

en.text: In this example, the same login-button style is repeated on five pages and Docs was missed. Follow the project's existing structure to move it into a shared component, then check each page for blue buttons and unexpected changes. Tell me where to edit the style next time.

references.title: 技术债概念简介
references.title_en: Introduction to the Technical Debt Concept

learning.assumes: You have seen duplicated code with wide change impact, or AI suggesting a later refactor.
learning.outcome: You can recognize a maintenance burden from repeated edits and missed changes, then decide whether to address it based on impact.

modules.title: From five repeated styles to one shared component

example.label: Compare repeated button styles before and after sharing

The button color now has one source.
steps.caption: Move the repeated style into a shared button component that fits the project's existing structure; all five pages use it.

steps.demo:
Five pages · verificationAs expected

DocsLog in · blue

steps.caption: Reopen all five pages to confirm the color is right and no other page behavior changed. A shared source reduces edit points; pages still need review.

items.title: Before: five files keep separate copies
items.text: Changing the button color means finding five definitions; miss Docs and its button stays gray.

items.title: The change: a shared component
items.text: Following the project's existing structure, put the button style in one shared component and let all five pages use it.

items.title: Feedback and boundary
items.text: Reopen all five pages and confirm the buttons are blue without changing other page behavior. Whether to consolidate more depends on the actual maintenance burden; not every repeated line needs rewriting.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: Not every repeated line needs consolidation. When a color update has already missed one page and still means finding five sources, the maintenance burden is visible. Before sharing an implementation, check whether any page needs its own style.

distinctions.label: Bug
distinctions.text: A bug is incorrect behavior to fix; technical debt is a maintenance burden that can exist even while the feature works.

distinctions.label: Refactoring
distinctions.text: Refactoring is the act of paying off debt; technical debt is the debt itself. Recording debt and paying it are two things.
